evidence_gaps: Notes reference captures are unavailable. The 17 usable references are Apple Reminders; no exact auth, Activity, capacity, medium-detent or combined-system-setting reference exists. Comparisons inform native spacing/type/behavior, not copied layouts.

The 808 matrix images are acquisitions across 29 families, not 808 distinct screens or independent quality votes: 398 XCTest acquisitions and 410 manual native acquisitions. Eighty protected XCTest keyboard frames are partial. Sixteen clean full-device normal/combined keyboard supplements plus eight populated-focus supplements provide additional evidence.

The separate final login set has 44 matched before/after states plus eight unmatched seeded filled/enabled inert previews. The latter have no exact S-before. The optional additional ordinary fully filled comparison stopped with a driver failure and produced zero frames; it is not passed evidence.

Ordinary offline fixtures disable external provider/legal actions. Enabled inert appearance previews show enabled paint but do not establish live authentication, web-sheet behavior, AutoFill or actual submission success.

True Lock Screen, physical-device haptics, spoken VoiceOver, AX1–AX5, live auth/recovery, and hardware interaction performance remain unobserved. These are confidence limits, not fabricated observed defects.

Nine recordings were reviewed through three distributed frames each on three inspection sheets. This is 27 sampled encoded frames, not continuous playback or a frame-time study. Five metrics samples are simulator Debug host XCTest only; no hardware or improvement claim follows.

Long native Activity evidence is light at default/XXXL; short native Activity covers light/dark and both sizes. Intentional tail ellipsis and intentionally empty compact/minimal regions are not defects.

Final source and captures are bound by the sourceIdentity/freeze manifest. Historical uncommitted/pack-blocked and earlier R/T/S failures remain acquisition history. The normalized checks and source-binding supersede those handoff-status flags without claiming a new capture. Parent acceptance is permission for independent grading, not user visual acceptance.

findings.screen: Default Sign In, light/dark, empty and filled
findings.description: The final opening is substantially clearer than its matched before, but Apple, Google, email input and submit still form a sequence of similarly wide, similarly prominent rectangles. The eye scans a stack of alternatives rather than a strongly composed first task. This is a taste judgment on actual default originals, not a clipping, target-size or contrast failure; passed geometry gates do not resolve it.
findings.fix: Prototype a substantive alternative default composition: a compact brand introduction followed by one contiguous email/helper/field/submit work area, with provider choices in a visibly secondary unboxed block below, separated by space or a hairline. Keep every original word, brand/icon, native Apple treatment, and at least 44-point targets. Compare default light/dark empty and filled renders side by side before selecting the composition; do not accept spacing adjustments alone as proof of polish.

check.performed: Independent original-pixel review of all 52 final login images and all 44 matched pairs; source structure inspected. No automated taste assertion was used.
check.required_regression: After any composition change, retain copy/provider integrity and native 44-point/XXXL/keyboard/contrast checks, rerun the existing iOS suite, and obtain a default-size visual comparison. This proposed change and its regression checks were not run.

findings.screen: Sign In submit loading state, default and XXXL
findings.description: The loading spinner increases submit height and moves the alternate action and legal footer downward. A read-only pixel scan at x=120 of the 3x native default captures found the same submit background from y=1430..1585 idle (156 px, 52 pt) and y=1430..1630 loading (201 px, 67 pt): a 15-point reflow. XXXL originals show approximately 21 points of growth. The source ZStack hides the label with opacity but lets the inherited large ProgressView enlarge intrinsic height.
findings.fix: Place a regular-sized spinner in a constrained overlay on the label’s existing layout footprint, rather than allowing ProgressView to size the ZStack. Preserve scaled multiline labels, loading accessibility text, disabled semantics, and the minimum touch target.
findings.basis: observed + source-derived; programmatically measured native pixels

check.performed: Read-only Python/Pillow native-pixel comparison: same light/dark default rounded-button fill run at x=120 was 156 px idle versus 201 px loading; dark XXXL was about 173 versus 234 px at that rounded-edge sample. This verifies reflow, not live animation timing.

Confirm spinner visibility and at least 44-point targets; rerun the existing iOS suite. New regression not run.

findings.title: XXXL password focus can leave its heading under navigation
findings.screen: Sign In, empty password focused, XXXL, normal dark and combined light
findings.observation: The first two clean full-device captures cut the upper part of Password at the hard navigation edge. The actual secure field and Done remain visible. The populated supplement positions the heading correctly, so the defect is inconsistent focus alignment rather than an unusable field.
findings.concrete_fix: Make focus scrolling prioritize the active field together with its heading, and only scroll farther to show submit/alternate controls when space permits. Avoid unconditionally using the alternate-action bottom as the focus anchor.
findings.confidence: high for observed alignment; medium for the proposed causal explanation
findings.check: Add a native regression capture/assertion for the heading and field bounds after first password focus and after keyboard dismissal/refocus at default and XXXL, both appearances and combined settings. Require both to clear the navigation edge; retain the existing strict SignInSurface checks and run the full iOS suite. Proposed check was not run by this reviewer.

findings.screen: Sign In, default and XXXL loading, both appearances
findings.observation: With the email group fixed in place, the loading submit rectangle becomes visibly taller and moves the alternate action and legal links down. The progress indicator is also large relative to the text it replaces.
findings.concrete_fix: Keep the text-derived button footprint stable and overlay a smaller native spinner that does not participate in intrinsic height, while retaining the accessible in-progress label and disabled semantics.
findings.check: Assert native submit bounds and alternate/legal vertical positions remain stable between filled, pending and settled states at default and XXXL. Capture both appearances and run the existing iOS suite; this new regression check has not been run.

findings.title: The default login provider pair has uneven visual weight
findings.screen: Sign In, default light enabled and filled
findings.observation: The custom Google outline is visibly heavier than the official Apple outline. Together with differently rounded filled fields and the prominent submit, the default screen still reads as several control treatments assembled into one stack, despite much better grouping.

findings.title: Account instructions remain difficult to scan at XXXL
findings.screen: Account, expanded widget guidance and persistence footer
findings.observation: The expanded instructions occupy three full-width paragraph rows followed by another long footer. Contrast and paragraph separation are improved, but action scanning still pauses for a large block of similarly weighted prose, especially at XXXL.
findings.concrete_fix: Preserve every word while giving the existing Home Screen and Lock Screen prefixes a modest semibold emphasis and clearer paragraph rhythm. Keep the current native section structure, disclosure and separate actions; do not add cards or lower helper contrast.
